title: Savings & Money Market Accounts: Posting Dates and the Day of Contact in Reactivations
content:
Reactivating a dormant Savings & Money Market Accounts product ties the account's new latest-activity date to a transaction of the owner's own within the present contact. This page explains how that link between the date and the contact is judged.

## What the recorded date must be

The date recorded is the posting date of the transfer the owner carries out in the present contact, as the ledger shows it for that withdrawal. It is never the date of a withdrawal from some earlier occasion, however recent that withdrawal looks on the ledger: an old transfer is not a transaction of this contact and cannot reactivate the account under this policy.

The ledger cannot tell which contact produced a transfer. Whether a transfer belongs to the present call is settled by the call, during which the owner performs it. Reactivation under this policy is available only on such a transfer; the date derived from the ledger carries no check of that point.

## The day of the contact

A withdrawal's posting date is always a business day, meaning Monday to Friday other than a Federal Reserve holiday. A transfer the owner makes on a Saturday, a Sunday or a Federal Reserve holiday is posted on the next business day, which comes after the contact; it therefore has not posted within the contact.

For that reason a reactivation date is established under this policy only when the posting date the ledger yields is no later than the current date, the day of the contact. A posting date later than the day of the contact means no reactivation date under this policy.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical contacts)

| Day of contact | Transfer posts on | Established? |
|---|---|---|
| Wednesday 9 October | Wednesday 9 October | yes, the posting date equals the day of contact |
| Saturday 12 October | Tuesday 15 October, the Monday being a Federal Reserve holiday in this example | no, the posting date is after the contact |
| Friday 11 October | Friday 11 October | yes |

## Points of judgement

**On a weekend call, may the next business day be recorded in advance?** No. The date has to be one on which the transfer has actually posted by the day of the contact; a date lying beyond it is not established.

**The ledger's latest telephone transfer is from last year. Does it date the reactivation?** No. That transfer belongs to an earlier occasion, not to this contact.
